description: Manages user accounts, roles, organizational unit settings, and provides capabilities for searching and updating user information within the system.

exampleCriteria.description: Find users whose name or email contains 'john.doe'
Filter users by a specific role, e.g., 'Administrator'
Filter users by their organizational unit code, e.g., 'HQ'
Show users only from the current user's organizational unit
Retrieve the first page of results
Set the number of results per page to 10

endpoints.name: GetUsers
endpoints.description: Retrieves a paginated list of users, supporting various filtering, searching, and sorting options. This endpoint allows for complex queries to find specific users or groups of users. Use the 'request' body to specify search criteria, pagination, and sorting preferences. For advanced search, provide criteria as a JSON array of objects, where each object has 'field', 'operator', and 'value'. Supported fields for search include: SearchTerm, RoleFilter, OrgUnitFilter, ShowMyOrgUnitOnly, PageIndex, PageSize, SortBy, SortDirection, OrderBy, Ascending, Direction. Supported operators are: like, is, not, contains, startsWith, between.

request.description: User management request with pagination and filters. Contains properties for search, filtering, sorting, and pagination.

request.SearchTerm.description: A general search term to find users by name, email, or other relevant fields.

request.RoleFilter.description: Filters users by a specific role.

request.ShowMyOrgUnitOnly.description: If true, only users from the current user's organizational unit will be returned.

request.OrgUnitFilter.description: Filters users by a specific organizational unit code.

request.SortBy.description: The field to sort the results by.

request.PageIndex.description: The current page number for pagination (0-indexed).

request.PageSize.description: The number of items to return per page.

example_uses: Find all users in the 'IT' department who are administrators, showing 20 per page.
List the first 10 users whose names contain 'smith' and are part of my organizational unit.
Retrieve a list of all active users, sorted by their last name in ascending order.
endpoints.when_to_use: Use this endpoint when you need to retrieve a list of users with specific criteria, such as filtering by role, organizational unit, or searching by a term, and require pagination for the results.

endpoints.name: GetUser
endpoints.description: Retrieves the detailed information for a single user identified by their unique user ID.

userId.description: The unique identifier of the user to retrieve.

example_uses: Get the profile details for user 'USR12345'.
Show me all information about the user with ID 'abc-def-ghi'.
Retrieve the contact details for the user 'johndoe@example.com'.
endpoints.when_to_use: Use this endpoint when you need to fetch the complete details of a specific user, given their user ID.

endpoints.name: UpdateUserRoles
endpoints.description: Updates the roles assigned to a specific user. This operation replaces the existing roles with the new set of roles provided in the request body.

userId.description: The unique identifier of the user whose roles are to be updated.

request.description: The request body containing the list of roles to assign to the user.

request.Roles.description: A list of role names (strings) to be assigned to the user. Existing roles not in this list will be removed.

example_uses: Assign 'Editor' and 'Publisher' roles to user 'USR987'.
Change user 'USR54321' roles to only 'Viewer'.
Update the roles for user 'jane.doe' to include 'Administrator' and 'Reporter'.
endpoints.when_to_use: Use this endpoint when you need to modify the roles associated with a particular user, either adding new roles or removing existing ones.

endpoints.name: GetAvailableRoles
endpoints.description: Retrieves a list of all roles that the current authenticated user is authorized to assign to other users. This is useful for populating role selection interfaces.
example_uses: What roles can I assign to new users?
List all the roles that are available for me to manage.
Show me the permissions I have to assign roles.
endpoints.when_to_use: Use this endpoint to get a list of roles that the current user has the authority to assign, typically for displaying options in a user management interface.

endpoints.name: GetCurrentUserOrgUnit
endpoints.description: Retrieves the organizational unit code associated with the currently authenticated user. This information can be used for filtering data or operations specific to the user's organizational context.
example_uses: What is my current organizational unit?
Get the organizational unit code for the logged-in user.
Determine which department I belong to.
endpoints.when_to_use: Use this endpoint to quickly get the organizational unit of the currently logged-in user, which can be helpful for contextual operations or displaying user-specific organizational information.

endpoints.name: GetOrgUnitSelfManagement
endpoints.description: Retrieves the self-management setting for a specific organizational unit. This setting indicates whether users within that unit are allowed to manage certain aspects of their own profiles or roles.

orgUnitCode.description: The unique code of the organizational unit to query.

example_uses: Check if self-management is enabled for the 'HR' organizational unit.
What is the self-management status of the 'Finance' department?
Retrieve the self-management setting for org unit 'EU-HQ'.
endpoints.when_to_use: Use this endpoint to check the current self-management configuration for a particular organizational unit.

endpoints.name: UpdateOrgUnitSelfManagement
endpoints.description: Updates the self-management setting for a specific organizational unit. This allows administrators to enable or disable self-management features for all users within that unit.

orgUnitCode.description: The unique code of the organizational unit to update.

request.description: The request body containing the new self-management setting.

request.IsSelfManagementEnabled.description: A boolean value indicating whether self-management should be enabled (true) or disabled (false) for the organizational unit.

example_uses: Enable self-management for the 'IT' organizational unit.
Disable self-management for the 'Sales' department.
Set the self-management status of org unit 'APAC' to true.
endpoints.when_to_use: Use this endpoint to change whether users within a specific organizational unit can manage their own settings or roles.
